children: The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note fell to 5.17% on Friday, following a sharp sell-off over the previous three sessions that pushed the benchmark yield up 23bps to around 5.20%.
A decline in oil prices, amid signs that US and Iranian negotiators may be exploring a phased agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, provided some relief to the bond market.
Despite the modest pullback, borrowing costs remain at 2007 highs, as markets continue to price in expectations that the Federal Reserve will need to tighten monetary policy further.
The odds of another 25bps rate hike at the Fed’s next meeting currently stand at around 70%, while swaps are pricing in three additional quarter-point rate increases over the next year.
Strong economic activity and concerns over the fiscal outlook have also weighed on Treasuries.
While demand at Tuesday’s 2-year Treasury auction was robust, the 5-year Treasury auction drew unexpectedly weak demand.

title: Treasury Yields Edge Lower But Remain at Multi-Year Highs
